oi.text: The following table summarizes revenue and operating income (loss) data by reportable segment:

opex.text: Independent contractors provide a tractor and a driver and are responsible for all operating expenses in exchange for a fixed payment per mile. We do not have the capital outlay of purchasing or leasing the tractor. The payments to independent contractors and the financing of equipment under operating leases are recorded in revenue equipment rentals and purchased transportation. Expenses associated with company owned equipment, such as interest and depreciation, and expenses associated with employee drivers, including driver compensation, fuel, and other expenses, are not incurred with respect to independent contractors. Obtaining equipment from independent contractors and under operating leases effectively shifts financing expenses from interest to "above the line" operating expenses, and as such, we evaluate our efficiency using net income margin, as well as operating ratio.

costs.text: Independent contractors provide a tractor and a driver and are responsible for all operating expenses in exchange for a fixed payment per mile. We do not have the capital outlay of purchasing or leasing the tractor. The payments to independent contractors and the financing of equipment under operating leases are recorded in revenue equipment rentals and purchased transportation. Expenses associated with company owned equipment, such as interest and depreciation, and expenses associated with employee drivers, including driver compensation, fuel, and other expenses, are not incurred with respect to independent contractors. Obtaining equipment from independent contractors and under operating leases effectively shifts financing expenses from interest to "above the line" operating expenses, and as such, we evaluate our efficiency using net income margin, as well as operating ratio.

nonop.heading: Interest expense, net
nonop.text:
The change in interest expense for the three months ended March 31, 2025 was insignificant both as a percentage of total revenue and freight revenue.

This line item will fluctuate based on our decision with respect to purchasing revenue equipment with balance sheet debt versus operating leases, our revenue equipment replacement plan, and changing interest rates.

tax.text: The effective tax rate is different from the expected combined tax rate due primarily to state tax expense and permanent differences. The rate impact of items such as executive compensation disallowance and the deductibility of per diem payments will fluctuate in future periods as income fluctuates.

net.text: We have accounted for our investment in TEL using the equity method of accounting and thus our financial results include our proportionate share of TEL's net income or loss. The change in TEL's contribution to our results for the three months ended March 31, 2025 was insignificant for the periods presented.

ocf.text: Net Cash flows provided by operating activities increased to $24.8 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025, compared to $21.7 million for the same 2024 period primarily due to an increase in net income of $2.6 million.

da.heading: Depreciation and amortization
da.text:
Depreciation and amortization consists primarily of depreciation of tractors, trailers, and other capital assets, as well as amortization of intangible assets.

Depreciation expense increased $0.6 million to $19.4 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to $18.7 million in the same 2024 period. Amortization of intangible assets was $2.4 million for each of the three months ended March 31, 2025 and 2024. Depreciation and amortization increased as a percentage of total revenue and freight revenue due to a decrease in total revenue and freight revenue compared to the 2024 period.

We expect depreciation and amortization to remain relatively similar to that of the first quarter of 2025, however, changes in the used tractor market have caused us to adjust residual values and increase depreciation, and further adjustments may be necessary in the future. These changes may also cause us to hold assets longer than planned, or experience increased losses on sale. Additionally, growth in our Expedited or Dedicated reportable segments could also increase depreciation and amortization going forward.

capex.text: For the periods presented, the decrease in loss on disposition of property and equipment, net for the three months ended March 31, 2025, was insignificant both as a percentage of total revenue and freight revenue.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
The decrease in total revenue for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to 2025 primarily resulted from a $4.9 million decrease in fuel surcharge revenue and a $6.4 million, $6.0 million, and $1.5 million decrease in Expedited and Managed Freight, and Warehousing freight revenue, respectively, partially offset by a $9.5 million increase in Dedicated freight revenue.

This line item will fluctuate based on our decision with respect to purchasing revenue equipment with balance sheet debt versus operating leases, our revenue equipment replacement plan, and changing interest rates.

tax.text: The effective tax rate is different from the expected combined tax rate due primarily to state tax expense and permanent differences. The rate impact of items such as executive compensation disallowance and the deductibility of per diem payments will fluctuate in future periods as income fluctuates.

net.text: We have accounted for our investment in TEL using the equity method of accounting and thus our financial results include our proportionate share of TEL's net income or loss. The change in TEL's contribution to our results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to equipment leasing growth with better lease rates and improvement in gain on sale of equipment as a result of improvements in the used equipment market. For the remainder of 2026, we expect TEL's earnings to remain relatively similar to those of the current period. However, due to TEL's business model, gains and losses on sale of equipment is a normal part of the business and can cause earnings to fluctuate from period to period and therefore our income from investment to similarly fluctuate.

ocf.text: Net cash flows provided by operating activities decreased to $44.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $88.1 million for the same 2025 period. Changes in operating assets and liabilities used $43.6 million and $3.7 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, largely due to an increase in the cash used for receivables and advances driven by an increase in our days sales outstanding of 51 days compared to 48 days in the 2025 period. Additionally net income decreased to $23.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $25.5 million for the same 2025 period. These increases in cash used during the 2026 period were partially offset by higher non-cash adjustments, including deferred income tax benefit and depreciation and amortization.

da.heading: Depreciation and amortization
da.text:
Depreciation and amortization consists primarily of depreciation of tractors, trailers, and other capital assets, as well as amortization of intangible assets.

Depreciation expense increased $0.2 million to $20.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and increased $1.2 million to $61.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 , compared to $20.3 million and $60.1 million in the same 2025 periods. Amortization of intangible assets was $3.0 million and $9.0 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $2.7 million and $7.8 million for the same 2025 periods. The increase for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 is due to the amortization of the intangible asset related to the Star Acquisition.

We expect depreciation and amortization to increase on a per unit basis going forward as the cost of new equipment increases. Additionally, changes in the used tractor market have caused us to adjust residual values and increase depreciation, and further adjustments may be necessary in the future. These changes may also cause us to hold assets longer than planned, or experience increased losses on sale. If we were to grow our Expedited or Dedicated reportable segments we may face additional increases in depreciation and amortization.

capex.text: For the periods presented, the change in (gain) loss on disposition of property and equipment, net was insignificant both as a percentage of total revenue and freight revenue.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
The increase in total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 2025 primarily resulted from a $49.4 million, $3.8 million, and $1.9 million increase in freight revenue for Managed Freight, Dedicated, and Warehousing, respectively, partially offset by a $9.6 million decrease in freight revenue for Expedited, as well as a $10.8 million increase in fuel surcharge revenue. The increase in total revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 2025 primarily resulted from a $105.3 million, $16.7 million, and $6.6 million increase in freight revenue for Managed Freight, Dedicated, and Warehousing, respectively, partially offset by a $27.4 million decrease in freight revenue for Expedited, as well as an $21.8 million increase in fuel surcharge revenue.

See results of reportable segment operations section for discussion of fluctuations.

For comparison purposes in the discussion below, we use total revenue and freight revenue (total revenue less fuel surcharge revenue) when discussing changes as a percentage of revenue.

For each expense item discussed below, we have provided a table setting forth the relevant expense first as a percentage of total revenue, and then as a percentage of freight revenue.

intro.text: Covenant Logistics Group, Inc., through its subsidiaries, offers a portfolio of transportation and logistics services to customers throughout the United States. Primary services include asset-based expedited and dedicated truckload capacity, as well as asset-light warehousing, transportation management, and freight brokerage capability. In addition, Transport Enterprise Leasing is an affiliated company providing revenue equipment sales and leasing services to the trucking industry. Covenant's Class A common stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol, “CVLG.” (1) See GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliation in the schedules included with this release.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
